evidence.reason: `boot()` spawns the child with `Popen(...)` at line 712, then writes the launch record at 714-715 before the `try` at 716. If `recorder.append()` raises (e.g., a write/OS error on the recorder), the exception escapes before the cleanup block, so the just-started `systemd-run` process (started in a new session, so it does not die with the CLI) is neither terminated nor reaped and can go on to launch QEMU after boot/scope cleanup has finished. The existing cleanup path (lines 730-753) already terminates and waits for `process`, so moving the record write inside the `try`, keeping it on the successful path, is the smallest compatible fix and does not change intended behavior. This is an ordinary error-handling ordering defect, not a proposal to add new scope or approval requirements.
